items.title: 4estGimp — Donated PDF Files (First 400 Sheets)
items.content:
4estGimp personally donated a PDF export of the first 400 entries from their comprehensive Fallout 4 patch and compatibility database to Mossy. This represents years of hands-on testing, patch creation, and community collaboration.

**Who is 4estGimp?**
4estGimp is one of Fallout 4's most prolific patch authors on Nexus Mods, with 100+ compatibility patches covering armor, weapons, settlements, NPCs, and gameplay systems. They are community-trusted for simplifying complex load orders.

**What the donated files contain (first 400 sheets):**

## Armor & Clothing Patches
- Compatibility patches resolving mesh, material, and keyword conflicts for armor mods
- Outfit/apparel mod bridges for AWKCR, ECO, and keywords frameworks
- Leveled list injection fixes for clothing overhauls

## Weapon Patches
- Munitions integration patches for weapon damage and ammo systems
- Keyword compatibility patches for weapon modding frameworks
- Crafting recipe conflicts and ECO (Equipment and Crafting Overhaul) fixes

## Settlement & Location Patches
- Precombine/previs conflict fixes for cell mods including Diamond City Outskirts and The Fens Empire
- Workshop framework and settlement build limit patches
- Sim Settlements 2 (SS2) compatibility bridges

## NPC & Faction Patches
- Raider Overhaul compatibility patches
- NPC appearance and replacement overhaul bridges
- Faction behavior and AI package conflict resolution

## Crafting & Economy Patches
- Equipment and Crafting Overhaul (ECO) integration patches
- Crafting menu conflict fixes
- Material and component keyword standardization patches

## Gameplay System Patches
- General bug fixes and feature-level integration patches
- Gameplay overhaul compatibility (survival, hardcore, difficulty mods)
- Framework bridges for keywords, scripts, and quest hooks

## Load Order Guidance
- Recommended placement for complex patch chains
- Plugin dependency notes
- Master file requirement documentation

**Live Database:** https://sheet.zohopublic.com/sheet/open/4gagib312c97873654347b49206d40f80afce
**Nexus Profile:** https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/users/30343500

items.title: 4estGimp — Patch List: Armor & Clothing Compatibility
items.content:
From 4estGimp's donated database (first 400 sheets). These are known armor and clothing compatibility patches by 4estGimp.

**DONATED BY 4estGimp — Nexus Mods: https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/users/30343500**

## Armor Patch Coverage
4estGimp's patches in the armor/clothing category address:
- **Keyword conflicts:** When two armor mods use conflicting AWKCR or vanilla keywords, patches align them so perks and crafting menus work correctly
- **Mesh/material conflicts:** When mods edit the same NIF or material file, causing visual glitches or CTDs
- **Leveled list injection:** When multiple armor mods inject into the same leveled lists, causing overpopulation or missing spawns
- **ECO (Equipment and Crafting Overhaul) compatibility:** Patches that make armor mods play nicely with ECO's crafting framework

## How to Find the Right Patch
1. Open the live Zoho Sheet: https://sheet.zohopublic.com/sheet/open/4gagib312c97873654347b49206d40f80afce
2. Search (Ctrl+F) for your armor mod name
3. Check the compatibility column for known patches
4. Download patches from 4estGimp's Nexus profile or the linked pages

## When Mossy Recommends 4estGimp Patches
If you're seeing armor-related conflicts (wrong textures, invisible pieces, CTD when wearing certain items, missing crafting options), Mossy will first check if 4estGimp has a patch for your specific combination. If a patch exists, Mossy will direct you to it before suggesting manual xEdit fixes.

## Weapon Patch Coverage
4estGimp's weapon patches address:
- **Munitions integration:** If you use Munitions (a popular ammo overhaul), 4estGimp has patches that make weapon mods use Munitions ammo types correctly instead of vanilla ammo
- **Weapon keyword conflicts:** Two weapon mods editing the same keyword records — patches standardize these so perks and modifications work across all weapons
- **ECO crafting:** Weapon mod recipes that conflict with ECO's crafting framework get bridged
- **Damage normalization:** Patches that align weapon damage values across overhaul mods

## Munitions Compatibility
Munitions is one of the most patch-hungry mods in Fallout 4. 4estGimp has created an extensive series of Munitions compatibility patches for weapons. If you see ammo type errors or weapons not using Munitions ammo:
1. Check 4estGimp's Nexus profile for a Munitions patch for your weapon mod
2. Check the live database sheet for the specific mod
3. If no patch exists, Mossy can help you create one in xEdit

items.title: 4estGimp — Patch List: Settlements, Locations & Precombines
items.content:
From 4estGimp's donated database (first 400 sheets). Settlement, location, and precombine/previs patches.

**DONATED BY 4estGimp — Nexus Mods: https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/users/30343500**

## Settlement & Location Patch Coverage
4estGimp's patches in this category address:

### Precombine/Previs Conflicts
One of the most common causes of FPS drops and visual glitches in Fallout 4 is mods that break precombined meshes (precombines) or previs data. 4estGimp creates patches that:
- Restore broken precombines for cell mods
- Merge conflicting previs data between location mods
- Fix the most common precombine-breaking combinations

Key mods patched include: **Diamond City Outskirts**, **The Fens Empire**, and various worldspace expansion mods.

### Sim Settlements 2 (SS2) Compatibility
4estGimp has patches bridging settlement mods with SS2:
- Plot placement conflicts (SS2 plots conflicting with added settlement objects)
- City plan compatibility
- Workshop menu conflict fixes

### Workshop Framework Patches
- Build limit conflict fixes
- Workshop keyword and script patches
- Settlement supply line compatibility

## When You Need a Precombine Patch
If you're experiencing FPS drops in specific areas that only happen with certain mod combinations, Mossy will check 4estGimp's database first. A precombine patch is often the fix.

**Credit: 4estGimp — all patches are their creation. Endorse their work on Nexus Mods!**

items.title: 4estGimp — Patch List: NPC, Faction & Raider Overhaul Compatibility
items.content:
From 4estGimp's donated database (first 400 sheets). NPC appearance, faction, and AI patches.

**DONATED BY 4estGimp — Nexus Mods: https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/users/30343500**

## NPC & Faction Patch Coverage

### Raider Overhaul Compatibility
**Raider Overhaul** (and its variants) is one of the most patch-hungry NPC mods because it edits hundreds of actor records. 4estGimp has created an extensive series of Raider Overhaul compatibility patches for:
- Other NPC/faction overhauls that edit the same raider characters
- Armor mods that change raider gear
- Combat AI mods that affect raider behavior
- Quest mods that involve raider encounters

### NPC Appearance Patches
When two NPC overhaul mods edit the same character's appearance, they conflict. 4estGimp's patches merge these conflicts so all changes apply correctly without one mod overwriting the other.

### Faction Behavior & AI
- AI package conflicts when mods edit faction combat behavior
- Faction relationship patches (who is friendly/hostile to whom)
- Dialog and quest hook patches for faction-altering mods

## How to Use These Patches
1. Identify which NPC/faction mods are conflicting (usually via xEdit)
2. Search 4estGimp's live database for both mod names
3. Download and install any available patches
4. Place patches AFTER both mods in your load order

**Credit: 4estGimp — all patches are their creation. Endorse their work on Nexus Mods!**

items.title: 4estGimp — How to Use the Live Patch Database
items.content:
4estGimp maintains a live Zoho Sheet database that is more comprehensive and up-to-date than any snapshot. This guide explains how to use it effectively.

**DONATED KNOWLEDGE — 4estGimp: https://www.nexusmods.com/fallout4/users/30343500**

## Accessing the Database

**Primary URL:** https://sheet.zohopublic.com/sheet/open/4gagib312c97873654347b49206d40f80afce?sheetid=0&range=B1565

The sheet is publicly accessible — no login required.

## Finding Patches

### Step 1: Search by Mod Name
1. Open the sheet in your browser
2. Press Ctrl+F (Windows) or Cmd+F (Mac) to open find
3. Type the name of the mod you're having issues with
4. Check every row that matches for the relevant patch

### Step 2: Read the Columns
The database typically includes:
- **Mod Name:** The mod being patched
- **Patch Name / Link:** The specific patch file
- **Requires:** What both mods need to have installed
- **Load Order Notes:** Where to place the patch
- **Notes:** Known issues, version requirements, special instructions

### Step 3: Download the Patch
- Most patches link directly to Nexus Mods
- Some are hosted on the Tortured Minds Discord
- Always download from the listed source

### Step 4: Install Correctly
- Install patches AFTER both parent mods in your load order
- Follow any specific load order notes in the database
- If using MO2, install as a separate mod and sort accordingly

## Getting Support
- **Tortured Minds Discord:** 4estGimp's primary support hub for patch requests and questions
- **Nexus Mod Pages:** Leave comments with issues found
- **MRC Catalogue:** https://resourcecatalogue.co.uk/4estgimp-user-files (browseable by category)

## Requesting New Patches
4estGimp does take patch requests through the Tortured Minds Discord. Be sure to include:
- Both mod names and version numbers
- The specific conflict (what breaks, what records conflict)
- An xEdit conflict report if you can generate one

**Credit: This guide is based on 4estGimp's donated knowledge. All patches are their creation.**
